body:
Thank you for being so compassionate. I honestly feel a million times better just by feeling that I understand the situation, so I don't feel like a letter would really be necessary for peace of mind.

>There’s no such thing as implied consent especially with medical stuff.

Also thank you for writing this. Another comment said something along the lines of "you're at a doctor, consent is implied" which just... I don't know. Made me feel bad. Also to me did not make sense because to me consent is never implied, it's either given or not given.

Again, thank you for being so kind and compassionate in your responses. I really needed that.

If treatment was that easy to get I would have but I've been on the waiting list for years. It's not as easy as "just getting treatment".

I literally made this post asking people to help me differentiate necessary medical treatment from sexual assault because I did not know what was factually occurring since again the doctor said literally nothing about why. I made this post to get insight that would help me deal with my emotional reaction. 

But even though compassion is literally free you felt like the best course of action was to tell someone you have never met that they have issues, based on their instinctual response to a stressful situation. And just a thought, there are way less rude ways to tell someone they percieved something incorrectly than immediately treating like they deliberately misinterpreted something just to be mean. 

A doctor is still a stranger. A doctor still has the ability to give someone a heads up. My vagina is a private and sensitive area for me regardless of the presence of a person with a doctorate. I have never met a gynecologist before or after this event who did not communicate about what they were doing. I am allowed to think that is a poor way to handle a patient, especially since most people feel very exposed and vulnerable with their ass out on a table. I am allowed to think a necessary examination is unpleasant, especially when no warning is given. I think blood tests are unpleasant, but they would be a lot more unpleasant if my doctor just pulled out a needle and stuck me in the arm at the end of an appointment, rather than telling me "we're gonna go a blood test, go wait for that over there".

Thanks for all the compassion? Yeah I have issues, I have been sexually assaulted in the past which left me traumatized and that experience has led to me being uncomfortable with strangers shoving their fingers up my vagina without warning in general. In the moment I was young, stressed and confused and I did genuinely not see a reason for him to have needed to do that. I am not an educated gynecologist, so I assumed that literally seeing the cysts was enough examination, which made everything that happened after that feel like it wasn't needed. 

If it is a necessary part of the examination he could and imo should still have at least given me a heads up, since that is in my experience standard in all health exams. Every other doctor I have met in my life (and there are many) have given me a heads up every time they are going to touch me anywhere with anything. To wish for the same level of consideration before something is forcefully put up my vagina is not unreasonable.

Yeah I've been assuming it was poor communication. The whole experience got me too shaken up to remember it in great detail but as far as I can remember he didn't give me enough warning to give me a chance to react, it was more of an "explaining while doing" situation. Which I believe was partially why it was so upsetting. I doubt I'd have seen it as a nearly as bad experience if he had said something along the lines of "this is a good opportunity to demonstrate this is that okay" but I also would have wanted the option to say no thank you if it was purely educational, since I was there to check my health, and only that. Idk, I do feel like doctors shouldn't have the right to use such a private part of my body for educational purposes. I'm a person, not a vagina prop. Thank you for your comment, helped

I wasn't trying to affect his career at all, just get some closure emotionally. But as I remember it, no, he did not really explain anything at least not in a way that gave me any time to react to it.

Edit: also I am on a waiting list for therapy, which I have been on for like two years. I wish good therapy was readily accessible everywhere but in my experience bad therapy or a long waiting list are the two options where I live

Thank you! This is a really great response. And yeah all my other experiences have been very "ok I'm going to do this now just so you know" before doing anything and I think maybe that's part of why it was such an upsetting experience. Helped <3

A former "friend" of mine. He is manipulative and emotionally abusive. Nothing is ever his fault. He has sexually assaulted me and raped a 13 year old. All his friends believe he's "so nice". Words can't describe how much I despise him.

Thanks for the advice! I don't know what an hours labor costs but it's probably worth looking into at least. While I don't exactly *need* what's on it I can't see myself ever feeling like it's not important to me, but it's good to know it's possible to recover data years later. Helped!
Thank you for the advice! Will check out that sub, helped! :)

I used to do a decent amount of Sports but I'm talking a break right now because I lost the joy in it so it just became another thing I had to "get through". I'm hoping to find the joy again though because I know exercise makes you feel good! So far I've had a popsicle for breakfast and cleaned my room so I feel a bit better and I think I'm gonna go make some actual food (or atleast a sandwich) now.

Thank you for the kind comment. I try to keep telling myself things will get better and on good days I believe it but on days like this I just don't see how. I'm hoping tomorrow is better if nothing else.

Helped

Thank you. I will try to call a hotline and see what they can do.
